reply:
A Graph is a set of Nodes and paths that controls a task. In this task, the Graph stops at a point where it waits for a confirmation. When it stops, it writes a Checkpoint. A Checkpoint is a saved record of the Graph state that helps the Graph continue.

The Checkpoint links the reply to the part of the task that is on hold. After the Graph starts again, the Node that comes next makes the report.

One limit is important here. A Checkpoint does not guarantee that an external action happens only once. So if the task crashes, the write to the external file can happen more than once. The Graph does not give an exactly-once guarantee for that file write after a crash.
